title: Invariant of a failure-free Goldreich–Levin run
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a Boolean function, and let $0<\tau\le 1$. For every $k\le n$ and every state-and-cost outcome in the support of the randomized query procedure run through stage $k$, if the state’s trace contains no estimate whose error in restricted Fourier weight is at least $\tau^2/4$, then there is an active family $\mathcal A$ of subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ such that the state records $\mathcal A$ as its active family, every member of $\mathcal A$ is contained in $\{0,\ldots,k-1\}$, and every Fourier coefficient of $f$ with magnitude at least $\tau$ has its intersection with $\{0,\ldots,k-1\}$ in $\mathcal A$. Moreover, when $k>0$, every $S\in\mathcal A$ has restricted Fourier weight greater than $\tau^2/4$ for the first $k$ coordinates and frequency $S\cap\{0,\ldots,k-1\}$, and $|\mathcal A|\le\lceil4/\tau^2\rceil$.
hypotheses_covered: Boolean target function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
stage index $k$ is a natural number with $k\le n$
